lines.text: This hexagon is cut into twenty-four little triangles.
lines.caption: This hexagon is cut into twenty-four little triangles.

lines.text: But bigger ones hide inside! How many in all?
lines.caption: But bigger ones hide inside! How many in all?

lines.text: A regular hexagon is cut into twenty-four small triangles.
lines.caption: A regular hexagon is cut into twenty-four small triangles.

lines.text: How many triangles of any size are in the figure?
lines.caption: How many triangles of any size are in the figure?

lines.text: Here's a shortcut. Count only the triangles pointing up.
lines.caption: Here's a shortcut. Count only the triangles pointing up.

lines.text: Twelve little ones, six medium ones, and one big one. That's nineteen pointing up.
lines.caption: Twelve little ones, six medium ones, and one big one. That's nineteen pointing up.

lines.text: Now flip the hexagon upside down. It looks the same, so there are nineteen pointing down too!
lines.caption: Now flip the hexagon upside down. It looks the same, so there are nineteen pointing down too!

lines.text: Counting by size is slow. Flipping is fast.
lines.caption: Counting by size is slow. Flipping is fast.

lines.text: Why only one big one? The full lesson counts every size, plus every trap.
lines.caption: Why only one big one? The full lesson counts every size, plus every trap.
